dictLead: Meanings of the eclipse words used on this site, from umbra and contacts to magnitude and path width.
dictNoResults: No matching words. Try a shorter search.
dictDefAltitude: How many degrees the Sun or Moon stands above the horizon (negative means below). 90° is overhead.
dictDefAnnular: A solar eclipse in which the Moon is too small in the sky to cover the Sun completely, leaving a bright ring (annulus) of sunlight.
dictDefAnnularity: The phase of an annular eclipse when the ring of sunlight is visible, between second and third contact (C2–C3).
dictDefAntumbra: The region of a shadow beyond the umbra, where the Moon does not fully cover the Sun. Observers there see an annular eclipse.
dictDefApparent: A direction or height as you see it, including the atmosphere bending light (refraction). Charts on this site use apparent altitude and azimuth.
dictDefAzimuth: Compass direction around the horizon: 0° is north, 90° east, 180° south, 270° west.
dictDefBesselian: NASA numbers that describe a solar eclipse’s geometry. Umbra uses them (via astronomy-bundle) to compute local solar circumstances. They are not used for lunar eclipses.
dictDefC1: Solar eclipse: the instant the Moon first nicks the Sun’s disk. The partial phase begins.
dictDefC2: Solar eclipse: the start of totality or annularity at your location (when those phases occur). Not listed for a purely partial eclipse.
dictDefC3: Solar eclipse: the end of totality or annularity at your location.
dictDefC4: Solar eclipse: the Moon leaves the Sun’s disk. The eclipse is over at your location.
dictDefCatalog: The list of eclipses on this site (1900–2100). Solar events come from NASA Besselian elements; lunar events from Espenak & Meeus (NASA GSFC).
dictDefCentral: The middle phase of a solar eclipse at your site: totality or annularity (C2 to C3). “Central duration” is how long that phase lasts. On lunar pages it means totality (U2 to U3).
dictDefCenterline: The track on Earth where a solar eclipse is most central (deepest totality or annularity). Shown in red on the map.
dictDefCircumstances: What the eclipse looks like at your chosen place: times, coverage, and whether it is visible. Global catalog type can differ from what you see locally.
dictDefCloudCover: The fraction of the sky covered by clouds, as a percent, from Open-Meteo. Forecasts cover about 16 days; earlier dates use the ERA5 archive (from 1940). Values are the nearest hour to each contact time.
dictDefContact: An instant when one disk (Moon, Sun, or Earth’s shadow) first touches or last leaves another. Labels are C1–C4 for solar eclipses and P1/U1–U4/P4 for lunar eclipses.
dictDefCoordinates: Latitude and longitude of the observer. Latitude is north/south; longitude is east/west.
dictDefCoverage: For solar eclipses, the fraction of the Sun’s area hidden by the Moon (obscuration), shown as a percent. Not the same as magnitude.
dictDefDuration: How long a phase lasts. Solar “total length” is first to last contact (C1–C4). “Central” is totality or annularity. Lunar pages show penumbral, umbral, and total durations from the catalog.
dictDefEclipse: When one body passes into another’s shadow. A solar eclipse is the Moon covering the Sun as seen from Earth. A lunar eclipse is Earth’s shadow falling on the Moon.
dictDefEgress: The second half of the eclipse, after greatest, as the shadow leaves. “Partial eclipse — after greatest” on the Now card.
dictDefElevation: Height of the observer above sea level, in metres. Taken from terrain data (Open-Meteo / Copernicus DEM) when you pick a place.
dictDefGamma: How far the shadow axis misses Earth’s (or the Moon’s) center, in Earth radii. Near 0 is central; larger values are more grazing. Sign indicates north or south of center.
dictDefGreatest: The instant the eclipse is deepest. For solar eclipses this is maximum coverage at your site (or globally on the facts card). For lunar eclipses it is the same worldwide, shown as Max.
dictDefHorizon: Altitude 0°. The Sun or Moon is “up” when altitude is positive. If it is below the horizon, that eclipse phase is not visible even if it is happening.
dictDefHybrid: A rare solar eclipse that is total along part of the path and annular along another part, because the Moon’s apparent size is right on the edge.
dictDefIngress: The first half of the eclipse, from first contact until greatest, as the shadow moves on.
dictDefLunarEclipse: The Moon passing through Earth’s shadow. Visible from the whole night side of Earth if the Moon is above the horizon. Open Lunar in the navigation.
dictDefMagnitude: For solar eclipses, the fraction of the Sun’s diameter covered by the Moon (not the area). 1.0 means the Moon’s disk just spans the Sun. Distinct from obscuration (area coverage).
dictDefMoonrise: When the Moon’s center crosses the horizon going up, at your location, around the eclipse.
dictDefMoonset: When the Moon’s center crosses the horizon going down, at your location, around the eclipse.
dictDefMoonSunRatio: Apparent diameter of the Moon divided by that of the Sun. Greater than 1 favors a total solar eclipse; less than 1 favors annular.
dictDefObscuration: Fraction of the Sun’s disk area covered by the Moon. This is the “coverage” percent on solar pages.
dictDefObserver: The place on Earth you chose (map tap, search, or GPS). All local times and coverage are computed for this point.
dictDefP1: Lunar eclipse: the Moon first enters Earth’s penumbra (light outer shadow). The penumbral eclipse starts.
dictDefP4: Lunar eclipse: the Moon leaves Earth’s penumbra. The eclipse is over.
dictDefPartial: Solar: the Moon covers only part of the Sun. Lunar: Earth’s umbra covers only part of the Moon. A global total can still be partial at your location.
dictDefPath: The region on Earth that sees a total or annular solar eclipse. Penumbra (blue), umbra/antumbra (dark), and centerline are drawn on the solar map. Lunar eclipses have no Earth path.
dictDefPathWidth: How wide the umbra or antumbra band is at your location, in kilometres. Zero if you are only in the partial zone or outside the eclipse.
dictDefPenumbra: The light outer part of a shadow. Solar: people in the penumbra see a partial eclipse. Lunar: the Moon in Earth’s penumbra looks only slightly dimmed.
dictDefPenumbralEclipse: A lunar eclipse in which the Moon only enters Earth’s penumbra, never the umbra. Umbral magnitude is 0 or negative; the shading is subtle.
dictDefPenumbralMagnitude: How deep the Moon goes into Earth’s penumbra, as a fraction of the Moon’s diameter. Used for penumbral lunar eclipses.
dictDefSaros: A cycle of about 18 years 11 days that groups similar eclipses into a family (Saros series). The number identifies which family an event belongs to.
dictDefSolarEclipse: The Moon passing in front of the Sun. Only visible from a limited path on Earth. Open Solar in the navigation.
dictDefStages: The contact times of the eclipse at your location, with a countdown to each. Solar uses C1–C4; lunar uses P1, U1–U4, and P4.
dictDefSunrise: When the Sun’s center reaches the horizon in the morning at your location, using apparent altitude (civil-style, not the Sun’s upper limb).
dictDefSunset: When the Sun’s center reaches the horizon in the evening at your location.
dictDefTimezone: The time zone of this device, used to display contact times (for example CET or UTC). Catalog dates stay in ISO form internally.
dictDefTotal: Solar: the Moon fully covers the Sun. Lunar: the Moon fully enters Earth’s umbra. Local type can be weaker than the catalog type if you are off the path or the Moon is low.
dictDefTotality: The phase when the Sun or Moon is completely in shadow: solar C2–C3, or lunar U2–U3. The sky can go dark (solar) or the Moon turn copper (lunar).
dictDefU1: Lunar eclipse: the Moon first enters Earth’s umbra (dark inner shadow). The partial umbral phase starts.
dictDefU2: Lunar eclipse: the Moon is fully inside Earth’s umbra. Totality starts. Missing on partial and penumbral eclipses.
dictDefU3: Lunar eclipse: the Moon begins to leave Earth’s umbra. Totality ends.
dictDefU4: Lunar eclipse: the Moon leaves Earth’s umbra. After this only the penumbral phase remains.
dictDefUmbra: The dark inner shadow. Solar: inside the umbra you see totality. Lunar: Earth’s umbra on the Moon is the dark bite (or full copper Moon). Also the name of this app.
dictDefUmbralMagnitude: How deep the Moon goes into Earth’s umbra, in Moon diameters. 0 is just grazing the umbra; 1.0 is just fully inside; above 1 is a deeper total lunar eclipse. Same everywhere on Earth.
dictDefVisible: Solar: the Sun is above the horizon during the eclipse at your site. Lunar: the Moon is above the horizon during the umbral phase (or during the penumbral phase if the eclipse is penumbral-only).
dictDefZenith: The point straight overhead. On the lunar map, the amber marker is where the Moon is at the zenith at greatest eclipse (night side of Earth).
